summary: Your own password server without writing a password manager: vaultwarden in Docker behind Caddy on HTTPS, the official Bitwarden apps and extensions pointed at it, signups closed after your account exists, an admin token done the way current vaultwarden requires, encrypted nightly backups off the box, and a restore you have actually performed before trusting it.

stack.why: rule zero: do not write a password manager

stack.choice: The official Bitwarden apps and extensions
stack.why: autofill, mobile and passkeys keep working because you did not rebuild them

stack.choice: tar plus age encryption, off the box
stack.why: a backup of every credential you own must be encrypted

prerequisites.name: A terminal and a code editor
prerequisites.why: Every step below is a command you type or a file you edit.
prerequisites.get: VS Code (code.visualstudio.com), Cursor or Zed. Open a folder for the project and use the editor's built-in terminal.
prerequisites.verify: You can open a folder and run a command in its terminal

prerequisites.name: Git
prerequisites.why: History for your code, and the way most hosts deploy.
prerequisites.get: Install from git-scm.com or with your package manager, then run git init in the project folder once it exists.

prerequisites.name: A small always-on server (VPS)
prerequisites.why: This needs one process running all the time with a public address. The vault must be reachable from your phone and laptops.
prerequisites.get: Hetzner Cloud (from about 4 EUR), DigitalOcean or Fly.io. Ubuntu 24.04, the smallest size. You need SSH access and a public IP. Only needed for the deploy phase; develop locally first.

prerequisites.name: Docker Engine and Compose on the VPS
prerequisites.get: docs.docker.com/engine/install/ubuntu, then add your user to the docker group.

prerequisites.name: A subdomain for the vault
prerequisites.why: The browser extensions and mobile apps refuse to talk to a non-HTTPS server; a domain is how you get a certificate.
prerequisites.get: vault.yourdomain.com, one A record to the VPS.
prerequisites.cost: free on a domain you own

prerequisites.name: age for backup encryption
prerequisites.why: Backups of your entire credential set must be encrypted at rest wherever they go.
prerequisites.get: apt install age, or from the releases page. Generate a key pair with age-keygen and keep the private key in your existing password manager.

prerequisites.name: An export of your current vault
prerequisites.why: Phase 5 imports it. Bitwarden exports are unencrypted by default; you will delete the file securely afterwards.
prerequisites.get: In your current manager: Export vault, JSON or CSV. Keep it only until import.

prerequisites.name: Off-box storage for backups
prerequisites.why: A backup on the server being backed up is not a backup.
prerequisites.get: Backblaze B2 or Cloudflare R2 plus rclone on the VPS.

env.name: DOMAIN
env.where: The exact public address; vaultwarden needs it for WebAuthn and links.

env.name: ADMIN_TOKEN
env.where: An Argon2 PHC hash from docker run --rm -it vaultwarden/server:latest /vaultwarden hash. In a Compose .env either single-quote the whole value or escape every $ as $$.

env.name: SIGNUPS_ALLOWED
env.where: true until your account exists, then false.

env.name: AGE_RECIPIENT
env.where: Your age public key, for encrypting backups.

phases.title: Bring it up behind HTTPS
phases.goal: The web vault over a valid certificate, data surviving a restart. Never run it on plain HTTP even briefly.

steps.do: Write docker-compose.yml with vaultwarden/server and a ./vw-data volume, port published on 127.0.0.1 only
Write the Caddyfile and point DNS
steps.detail: vault.yourdomain.com with reverse_proxy localhost:80 (the container's port).

check: The web vault loads over HTTPS with a valid certificate
docker compose down && up keeps the data
traps: The clients will not connect over HTTP and you will spend the time debugging the wrong layer.

phases.title: The admin token
phases.goal: The step that wastes an evening, done right.

steps.detail: Single-quote the whole value, or escape each $ as $$; Compose otherwise interprets them as variables.

steps.do: Log in at /admin with the original password you typed, not the hash

check: /admin accepts the original password and rejects a wrong one
The value survives docker compose up without Compose mangling it

phases.title: Lock it down
phases.goal: One account, signups closed, nothing else exposed.

steps.do: Register your account, then set SIGNUPS_ALLOWED=false and restart
Confirm only 80 and 443 are reachable from outside

check: A fresh browser cannot reach a registration form
A port scan shows only 80 and 443

phases.title: Clients
phases.goal: Extension, desktop and mobile all logged in to your server.

steps.do: Log in the browser extension and the desktop app, choosing self-hosted and entering your server URL before login
Log in the mobile app and test a passkey and autofill end to end

check: Autofill works on a real site
An item created on the phone appears in the extension

phases.title: Import
phases.goal: Everything moved, and the plaintext export gone.

steps.do: Import through Tools > Import in the web vault
Securely delete the export file and empty the trash

check: Item counts match before and after
TOTP seeds still generate correct codes
The export file is gone from disk and trash

phases.title: Backup, and a restore drill
phases.goal: Encrypted nightly backup off the box, and a restore you performed.

steps.do: Write backup.sh: stop or snapshot, tar vw-data, encrypt with age, copy off
commands: docker compose stop && tar czf - vw-data | age -r $AGE_RECIPIENT -o /tmp/vw-$(date +%F).tgz.age && docker compose start

steps.do: Restore into a throwaway instance and unlock the restored vault with a client

check: Last night's encrypted backup exists off the box
A restore into a clean environment unlocks with a client
The restore date is written in the README
traps: Until the restore drill is done, keep the hosted subscription.

phases.title: Updates and the honest handover
phases.goal: A repeatable update and the trade written down.

steps.do: Write update.sh: backup, pull, up -d, verify login

steps.detail: The admin-token command and the $$ trap, the restore date, and the reassurance plus warning: clients cache the vault so a dead server locks you out of nothing, but an unpatched server holding every credential is a risk you took on.

check: One upgrade cycle run and all three clients still log in
The README carries the token trap and the restore date

product.outcome: A credential server you operate responsibly: closed signups, encrypted off-box backups with a proven restore, and a monthly patch routine.

architecture.swap: Any reverse proxy with automatic certificates

operations.backup: Nightly encrypted tar off the box, thirty kept.
operations.restore: restore.sh into a clean stack; unlock with a client.
operations.monitoring: Uptime on the domain; a monthly reminder to run update.sh.
operations.incident: Suspected compromise: rebuild the VPS from compose, restore the last known-good backup, rotate every credential in the vault starting with email.

notIncluded: Emergency access, organizations and family sharing.
Pretending you have a security team.
after: A second admin device with hardware-key 2FA on your account
Fail2ban in front of the login endpoint
